correctness.rationale: Exactly decompose \(L\) into orthogonal matching-edge projectors and the trivial projector. Ordinary off-diagonal entries obey \(T(h)_{ij}=12h/D_n(h)>0\). Each exceptional pair obeys \(T(h)_{ab}=6h Q_{n,t}(h)/(D_n(h)D_{\lambda}(h))\), where \(Q_{n,t}(h)=\lambda[n^2-(n-2)\lambda]h^2+12\lambda h+24t\) and \(\lambda=n-2+2t>0\). The quadratic coefficient has exactly the sharp sign claimed; the linear and constant coefficients are positive. Beyond the cutoff there is precisely one positive root. Since \(F(x)=((x-3)^2+3)/(x^2+6x+12)>0\) for \(x\ge0\), the transition is positive definite and all diagonal entries are positive. \(F(0)=1\) conserves row sums. The two-vertex exception follows directly. Independent exact-rational matrix checks supplement rather than replace the symbolic all-size proof.

originality.rationale: The first-public 2013 study of rational absolute monotonicity analyzes scalar stability-function criteria, not the sharp all-timestep threshold for individually perturbed edges of a dense graph. Earlier accessible unweighted complete/multipartite and weighted path/star results fail to imply this independently weighted matching family. Actual published-finding corpus and literature searches returned no direct equivalent or broader covering statement; unindexed specialist sources remain a residual risk.

value.rationale: Edge conductance perturbations of a complete mixing network are a motivated robustness model. The classification covers an arbitrary-size matching of independently selected positive conductances, proves the surprising independence of all threshold tests, gives a sharp dimension-dependent boundary tending to 2, and identifies a unique finite sign-reversal time for each supercritical edge. This is a natural complete classification and positivity-versus-stability contrast, not a parameter substitution or isolated tiny numerical gain.
